items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: mitigate

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The new drainage system is expected to ______ the risk of flooding in low-lying districts, although it cannot remove that risk completely."

explanation.en: "Mitigate" means to make something less serious, which fits a system that reduces the risk without removing it. "Eliminate" (remove completely) contradicts "cannot remove that risk completely"; "aggravate" means make worse; "neglect" means ignore.
explanation.th: mitigate แปลว่า ทำให้รุนแรงน้อยลง ตรงกับระบบที่ลดความเสี่ยงได้แต่ขจัดไม่หมด ส่วน eliminate (ขจัดให้หมด) ขัดกับ cannot remove completely, aggravate คือทำให้แย่ลง, neglect คือละเลย

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: inherent

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Some degree of uncertainty is ______ in any scientific measurement; no instrument is perfectly precise."

explanation.en: "Inherent" means existing as a natural, permanent part of something: uncertainty is built into every measurement because no instrument is perfect. "Incidental" means minor or accidental, "inferior" means lower in quality and "inhibited" means held back.
explanation.th: inherent แปลว่า มีอยู่โดยธรรมชาติในตัวสิ่งนั้น ความคลาดเคลื่อนมีอยู่ในการวัดทุกครั้งเพราะไม่มีเครื่องมือใดสมบูรณ์ ส่วน incidental = เล็กน้อย/โดยบังเอิญ, inferior = ด้อยกว่า, inhibited = ถูกยับยั้ง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: subsequently

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The data were first collected in 2015 and ______ analysed by a second team, who reached a different conclusion."

explanation.en: "Subsequently" means afterwards: the data were collected first and analysed later. "Previously" (before) and "simultaneously" (at the same time) break the time order; "consequently" means "as a result", which does not describe a later step by another team.
explanation.th: subsequently แปลว่า ต่อมาภายหลัง ข้อมูลเก็บก่อนแล้วจึงวิเคราะห์ทีหลัง ส่วน previously (ก่อนหน้า) และ simultaneously (พร้อมกัน) ผิดลำดับเวลา และ consequently แปลว่า ผลที่ตามมาคือ ไม่ได้บอกลำดับขั้นตอน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: consent

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำนาม

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Researchers must obtain the ______ of participants before including them in a study."

explanation.en: "Consent" is permission, which researchers must get from participants. "Consensus" is general agreement within a group, "content" is what something contains and "contempt" is a feeling of disrespect.
explanation.th: consent แปลว่า ความยินยอม ซึ่งนักวิจัยต้องได้จากผู้เข้าร่วม ส่วน consensus = ความเห็นพ้องของกลุ่ม, content = เนื้อหา, contempt = การดูหมิ่น

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: ambiguous

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The committee's report was deliberately ______, so readers on both sides of the debate believed it supported their view."

explanation.en: "Ambiguous" means open to more than one interpretation, which is why both sides could read it as support. An "explicit" report would be clear; "concise" only means short; "unanimous" describes agreement among people, not the wording of a text.
explanation.th: ambiguous แปลว่า กำกวม ตีความได้หลายแบบ ทั้งสองฝ่ายจึงคิดว่ารายงานสนับสนุนตน ส่วน explicit = ชัดเจน, concise = กระชับ, unanimous = เป็นเอกฉันท์ (ใช้กับความเห็นของคน)

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: undermined

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Critics argued that the survey's small sample ______ the reliability of its conclusions."

explanation.en: "Undermined" means weakened gradually; a small sample makes conclusions less reliable. "Reinforced" is the opposite, "underwent" (experienced) needs a process as its object, and "underlined" means emphasised.
explanation.th: undermined แปลว่า บั่นทอน ทำให้อ่อนลง กลุ่มตัวอย่างเล็กทำให้ข้อสรุปน่าเชื่อถือน้อยลง ส่วน reinforced = เสริมให้แข็งแรง (ความหมายตรงข้าม), underwent = ผ่าน/ประสบ, underlined = เน้นย้ำ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: distinct

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Although the two species look almost identical, they are genetically ______ and cannot interbreed."

explanation.en: "Distinct" means clearly different; the contrast with "look almost identical" and "cannot interbreed" requires it. "Indistinct" (unclear) does not fit, "extinct" species no longer exist, and "instinctive" describes behaviour.
explanation.th: distinct แปลว่า แตกต่างกันชัดเจน ซึ่งขัดแย้งกับ look almost identical ตามที่ although ต้องการ ส่วน indistinct = ไม่ชัด, extinct = สูญพันธุ์, instinctive = ตามสัญชาตญาณ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: concrete

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The minister's speech was full of vague promises; it lacked any ______ proposals for reducing unemployment."

explanation.en: "Concrete" means specific and practical, the opposite of "vague". The speech lacked specific proposals. "Abstract" and "implicit" describe things that are not clearly stated, so a vague speech would not lack them; "rhetorical" refers to persuasive language.
explanation.th: concrete ในที่นี้แปลว่า เป็นรูปธรรม ชัดเจน ตรงข้ามกับ vague สุนทรพจน์จึงขาดข้อเสนอที่เป็นรูปธรรม ส่วน abstract (นามธรรม) และ implicit (โดยนัย) เป็นลักษณะของคำพูดคลุมเครืออยู่แล้ว และ rhetorical หมายถึงเชิงวาทศิลป์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: gradual

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Rather than being a sudden event, the decline of the empire was a ______ process that took several centuries."

explanation.en: "Gradual" means happening slowly over time, matching "took several centuries" and contrasting with "sudden". "Abrupt", "spontaneous" and "momentary" all suggest something quick or unplanned.
explanation.th: gradual แปลว่า ค่อยเป็นค่อยไป ตรงกับ took several centuries และตรงข้ามกับ sudden ส่วน abrupt (กะทันหัน), spontaneous (เกิดขึ้นเอง) และ momentary (ชั่วขณะ) ล้วนสื่อความรวดเร็ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: correlation

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำนาม

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The study found a strong ______ between hours of sleep and exam performance, but it could not prove that one caused the other."

explanation.en: A "correlation" is a statistical relationship between two variables, which does not by itself prove cause and effect—exactly the point of the second clause. "Collaboration" is working together, "contradiction" is disagreement and "conclusion" does not take "between".
explanation.th: correlation คือ ความสัมพันธ์ทางสถิติระหว่างสองตัวแปร ซึ่งไม่ได้พิสูจน์ว่าสิ่งหนึ่งเป็นสาเหตุของอีกสิ่ง ตรงกับประโยคหลัง ส่วน collaboration = การร่วมมือ, contradiction = ความขัดแย้ง, conclusion = ข้อสรุป

items.subject: eng

skill.th: อนุประโยคลดรูปแบบ passive (V3)

topic.th: อนุประโยคลดรูปและวลี participle

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"______ in 1928, penicillin was not produced on a large scale until the 1940s."

explanation.en: Penicillin was discovered (passive), so the reduced clause uses the past participle "Discovered". "Having discovered" and "Discovering" are active, making penicillin the discoverer; "It was discovered" creates two main clauses with no linking word.
explanation.th: เพนิซิลลินถูกค้นพบ จึงใช้รูป passive ลดรูปเป็น Discovered ส่วน Having discovered และ Discovering เป็น active ทำให้เพนิซิลลินเป็นผู้ค้นพบ และ It was discovered ทำให้มีสองประโยคหลักโดยไม่มีคำเชื่อม

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Mandative subjunctive after 'It is essential that'
skill.th: subjunctive หลัง It is essential that

topic.th: subjunctive และประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"It is essential that every participant ______ informed of the risks before the experiment begins."

explanation.en: After "It is essential that", formal English uses the base-form subjunctive: "be informed". "Will be" and "has been" are indicative forms, and "being" cannot be the main verb of the clause.
explanation.th: หลัง It is essential that ภาษาทางการใช้ subjunctive คือกริยารูปพื้นฐาน be informed ส่วน will be และ has been เป็นรูปบอกเล่าธรรมดา และ being เป็นกริยาแท้ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: โครงสร้างคู่ขนานของกริยาในรายการ

topic.th: โครงสร้างคู่ขนาน (parallelism)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The new curriculum aims to improve students' critical thinking, strengthen their research skills, and ______."

explanation.en: The list after "aims to" contains bare verbs: improve, strengthen and "encourage". Parallel structure requires the same form, so "encourage independent learning". The -ing form, the noun phrase and the clause all break the pattern.
explanation.th: รายการหลัง aims to ใช้กริยารูปพื้นฐาน improve, strengthen จึงต้องเป็น encourage independent learning ให้ขนานกัน ส่วนรูป -ing, นามวลี และอนุประโยค ทำให้โครงสร้างไม่ขนาน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: noun clause ขึ้นต้นด้วย whether ทำหน้าที่ประธาน

topic.th: noun clause (อนุประโยคนาม)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"______ the universe will continue to expand forever remains one of the central questions of cosmology."

explanation.en: The clause is the subject and expresses a yes/no question, so it must begin with "Whether". "If" cannot introduce a subject clause, "That" presents it as a fact rather than a question, and "What" would need a missing noun inside the clause.
explanation.th: อนุประโยคนี้เป็นประธานและเป็นคำถามแบบใช่/ไม่ใช่ จึงต้องขึ้นด้วย Whether ส่วน If ใช้ขึ้นต้นอนุประโยคที่เป็นประธานไม่ได้ That ทำให้เป็นข้อเท็จจริงแทนคำถาม และ What ต้องมีส่วนที่ขาดหายในอนุประโยค

items.subject: eng

skill.th: inversion หลัง Not until

topic.th: การสลับที่ประธานกับกริยา (inversion)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Not until the late nineteenth century ______ that bacteria cause many common diseases."

explanation.en: A sentence that begins with "Not until …" needs question-like word order in the main clause: auxiliary + subject + verb, so "did scientists widely accept". The normal order is wrong here, and the other two choices put the words in an impossible order.
explanation.th: ประโยคที่ขึ้นด้วย Not until ต้องสลับเป็นรูปคำถามในประโยคหลัก คือ กริยาช่วย + ประธาน + กริยา จึงเป็น did scientists widely accept ส่วนการเรียงแบบปกติผิด และอีกสองแบบเรียงคำผิดหลัก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: appositive (นามวลีขยายนาม)

topic.th: appositive และ relative clause

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Marie Curie, ______, remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences."
choices: was a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw
who a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw
she was a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw
a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw

explanation.en: Between the commas we need an appositive: a noun phrase that renames Marie Curie, "a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw". "Who" would need a verb ("who was"), and the two choices with "was" create a second verb that cannot fit inside the main clause.
explanation.th: ระหว่างจุลภาคต้องเป็น appositive คือ นามวลีที่อธิบาย Marie Curie ได้แก่ a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw ส่วน who ต้องตามด้วยกริยา (who was) และแบบที่มี was ทำให้มีกริยาแท้ซ้อนในประโยค

items.subject: eng

skill.th: หลีกเลี่ยงส่วนขยายลอย

topic.th: ส่วนขยายลอย (dangling modifier)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"After analysing the results of the survey, ______."
choices: the researchers concluded that the policy had failed
the conclusion was that the policy had failed
it was concluded by the researchers that the policy had failed
the policy was found to have failed

explanation.en: The subject of the main clause must be the people who analysed the results. Only "the researchers concluded that the policy had failed" does this; the other choices make "the conclusion", "it" or "the policy" the doer of the analysing.
explanation.th: ประธานของประโยคหลักต้องเป็นผู้ที่วิเคราะห์ผลสำรวจ ซึ่งมีเพียง the researchers concluded that the policy had failed ส่วนแบบอื่นทำให้ the conclusion, it หรือ the policy กลายเป็นผู้วิเคราะห์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: relative clause ลดรูปแบบ active (V-ing)

topic.th: อนุประโยคลดรูปและวลี participle

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Most of the plastic ______ into the ocean each year comes from land-based sources rather than ships."

explanation.en: "Entering" is a reduced form of "that enters" and describes the plastic. "Enters" would give the sentence two main verbs, "is entered" is a wrong passive, and "to have entered" does not fit a general, repeated action.
explanation.th: entering คือรูปลดของ that enters ใช้ขยาย plastic ส่วน enters ทำให้มีกริยาแท้สองตัว is entered เป็น passive ที่ผิดความหมาย และ to have entered ไม่เข้ากับเหตุการณ์ที่เกิดซ้ำทุกปี

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขแบบผสม

topic.th: subjunctive และประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"If the bridge ______ according to the original design, it would still be standing today."

explanation.en: The building happened in the past, but the result ("would still be standing today") is in the present, so this is a mixed conditional: past perfect in the if-clause, "had been built". "Were built" and "was built" refer to the present or are not unreal, and "would" does not belong in the if-clause.
explanation.th: การสร้างสะพานเกิดในอดีตแต่ผลอยู่ในปัจจุบัน จึงเป็นเงื่อนไขแบบผสม ใช้ past perfect ใน if-clause คือ had been built ส่วน were built และ was built ไม่ได้อ้างถึงอดีตที่ไม่จริง และไม่ใช้ would ใน if-clause

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเปรียบเทียบแบบ twice as ... as

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องประธาน–กริยาและการเปรียบเทียบ

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The population of the city is now twice ______ it was in 1990."

explanation.en: Multipliers such as "twice" use "as … as": "twice as large as". "Twice larger than" is not standard in careful writing, "as large than" mixes two patterns, and "twice the size as" should be "twice the size of".
explanation.th: คำบอกจำนวนเท่า เช่น twice ใช้กับ as ... as จึงเป็น twice as large as ส่วน twice larger than ไม่ใช่รูปมาตรฐาน as large than ผสมสองโครงสร้าง และ the size ต้องตามด้วย of

items.subject: eng

skill.th: noun clause ทำหน้าที่กรรม (why)

topic.th: noun clause (อนุประโยคนาม)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The researchers could not explain ______ some patients recovered faster than others."

explanation.en: The clause after "explain" is complete (subject + verb + comparison), and the missing idea is the reason, so "why" is needed. "What" and "which" would need a gap in the clause, and "whose" needs a following noun.
explanation.th: อนุประโยคหลัง explain สมบูรณ์แล้ว สิ่งที่ขาดคือเหตุผล จึงใช้ why ส่วน what และ which ต้องมีช่องว่างในอนุประโยค และ whose ต้องตามด้วยคำนาม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: inversion หลัง So + adjective

topic.th: การสลับที่ประธานกับกริยา (inversion)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"So rapid ______ that many species have been unable to adapt."
choices: was being the change in climate
has the change in climate been
the change in climate has been

explanation.en: When "So + adjective" begins a sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject: "So rapid has the change in climate been that …". The normal order is wrong after a fronted "So rapid", and the other two choices have no correct finite verb.
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นประโยคด้วย So + adjective ต้องนำกริยาช่วยไว้หน้าประธาน คือ has the change in climate been ส่วนการเรียงปกติผิดในโครงสร้างนี้ และอีกสองแบบไม่มีกริยาแท้ที่ถูกต้อง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ใช้ number of กับนามนับได้

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องประธาน–กริยาและการเปรียบเทียบ

items.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be changed for the sentence to be correct.
The [[amount of]] students applying for science scholarships [[has risen]] steadily [[over]] the past decade, [[according to]] the ministry.

explanation.en: "Students" is a countable plural noun, so it takes "number of", not "amount of" (used with uncountable nouns). "The number of … has risen" is then correct.
explanation.th: students เป็นนามนับได้ จึงต้องใช้ number of ไม่ใช่ amount of (ใช้กับนามนับไม่ได้) และ The number of ... has risen ถูกต้อง

items.passage:
Sleep and the Making of Memories

For much of the twentieth century, sleep was regarded as a passive state: the brain, it was assumed, simply switched off for the night and recovered from the efforts of the day. Over the past few decades, however, this view has been largely abandoned. Researchers now believe that sleep plays an active role in learning, and in particular in the process known as memory consolidation, by which fragile new memories are transformed into stable, long-lasting ones.

Some of the most persuasive evidence comes from studies in which participants learn a task, such as a list of word pairs or a sequence of finger movements, and are then tested after a period of either sleep or wakefulness. Again and again, those who have slept perform better, even when the two periods are of equal length. Crucially, the advantage does not seem to come merely from being rested. Participants who learn in the evening and sleep immediately afterwards tend to outperform those who learn in the morning and are tested in the evening, although both groups are equally alert at the time of testing.

Recordings of brain activity have suggested a possible mechanism. During deep, slow-wave sleep, the hippocampus, a region essential for forming new memories, appears to "replay" patterns of activity that occurred during learning. These replays are thought to strengthen connections in the cortex, where long-term memories are eventually stored. In experiments with rats that had explored a maze, the same sequences of neurons that fired as the animals ran were observed firing again, in compressed form, while they slept.

Not all findings fit neatly into this picture. Some studies have found only small benefits of sleep for certain kinds of memory, and the size of the effect varies considerably between individuals. It also remains unclear whether different stages of sleep support different kinds of learning, as some researchers have proposed. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, for example, has been linked to emotional memory and creative problem-solving, but the evidence is less consistent than for slow-wave sleep.

Nevertheless, the practical implications are hard to ignore. Students who stay up all night before an examination may be sacrificing precisely the process that would help them retain what they have studied. A night without sleep after learning appears to impair recall even when the lost sleep is "made up" on the following nights, which suggests that the timing of sleep, and not simply its total amount, matters. For anyone whose work depends on learning, sleep may be less a luxury than a part of the job itself.
items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
choices: the reasons why students should avoid studying in the evening
how rats learn to find their way through mazes
the differences between REM sleep and slow-wave sleep
evidence that sleep actively helps the brain to store new memories

explanation.en: The passage moves from the old view of sleep as passive to research showing that sleep helps consolidate memories, so the main topic is "evidence that sleep actively helps the brain to store new memories". REM sleep and the rat experiment are only supporting details, and the passage actually reports good results for evening learners.

Why Witnesses Hesitate

Common sense suggests that a person in trouble is more likely to receive help when many people are around: the more witnesses there are, the greater the chance that at least one of them will act. Yet a large body of research in social psychology points to a different conclusion. In many situations, the presence of other people makes each individual less likely to intervene, a phenomenon known as the bystander effect.

In a classic series of experiments conducted in the late 1960s, participants were placed in situations that appeared to be genuine emergencies. In one version, a participant filling in a questionnaire noticed smoke entering the room through a vent. When alone, most participants left to report the smoke within a few minutes. When they sat with two other people who had secretly been instructed to ignore it, the majority continued working, waving the smoke away from their faces, for the entire session.

Psychologists have offered several explanations for this pattern. The first is the diffusion of responsibility. When a person is the only witness, the responsibility to act falls entirely on him or her; when there are many witnesses, it is shared, and each person feels it less heavily. A second explanation concerns the way people interpret ambiguous situations. Faced with uncertainty, we tend to look at others to decide how to behave. If everyone else appears calm, each observer concludes that nothing serious is happening, even though the others may be equally uncertain and simply hiding their concern. A third factor is the fear of embarrassment: intervening in front of an audience carries the risk of appearing foolish if the situation turns out not to be an emergency after all.

It would be a mistake, however, to conclude that crowds are always indifferent. A large review of studies published in 2011 found that the bystander effect is weaker when the danger is obvious and severe, perhaps because there is no ambiguity to resolve and because a group can share the physical risk of intervening. More recently, researchers analysing video footage of real public conflicts in several countries found that in the great majority of cases at least one bystander did intervene, and that the likelihood of someone helping increased as the number of bystanders rose.

These findings do not so much contradict the earlier research as refine it. The bystander effect describes how the probability that any single individual will help changes in a group; it does not mean that groups as a whole are unhelpful. Knowing about the effect may itself offer some protection. People who have learned about it, studies suggest, are more likely to recognise the moment of hesitation for what it is and to step forward.
items.stem: What is the author's main purpose in the passage?
choices: to persuade readers to take courses in social psychology
to explain a psychological effect and show how later research has qualified it
to describe the design of a single famous experiment in detail
to argue that people in crowds are generally unwilling to help strangers

explanation.en: The author defines the bystander effect, explains its causes, then reports newer studies that "refine" it. That is to explain the effect and show how later research has qualified it. The author explicitly rejects the idea that crowds are always unhelpful.

items.passage:
More Roads, More Traffic

When a busy road becomes congested, the obvious solution seems to be to build more lanes. If a road that carries 4,000 vehicles an hour is widened to carry 6,000, the reasoning goes, traffic will flow freely and journey times will fall. Yet transport economists have observed for decades that this reasoning often fails in practice. Within a few years of a road being widened, it is frequently just as congested as before. The explanation lies in a concept known as induced demand.

Demand for road space, like demand for most goods, depends partly on its price. The price of a car journey is not only the cost of fuel; it also includes the time the journey takes. When a road is congested, this time cost is high, and many potential trips are never made. Some people travel at quieter hours, some use public transport, some combine errands, and some simply decide that a trip is not worth the effort. Adding capacity lowers the time cost of driving, at least at first, and these "suppressed" trips begin to appear. People who used to take the train switch to driving, others move to houses further from their workplaces, and businesses locate along the improved route. Gradually the new space fills up.

A widely cited study of American cities found that between the 1980s and the 2000s the total distance driven increased almost exactly in proportion to the length of new roads built. In other words, a 10 percent increase in road capacity was associated with roughly a 10 percent increase in driving. The researchers concluded that building roads is unlikely to be an effective long-term remedy for congestion, at least in large cities where demand is high.

The idea also works in reverse. When roads are closed or their capacity is reduced, the chaos that planners predict often fails to materialise. Some of the traffic, sometimes called "evaporated" traffic, simply disappears as people change their routes, times or means of travel. Several cities that have removed elevated highways and replaced them with parks or boulevards have reported that overall traffic in the area decreased rather than spilling onto neighbouring streets.

None of this means that new roads are never justified. A road connecting two towns that previously had no direct link may bring considerable economic benefits, and in rural areas where demand is low, extra capacity may indeed reduce delays. But in dense urban areas, many economists argue that congestion is better managed by pricing road use directly, for example through charges for driving into city centres at peak times, and by investing in alternatives that allow people to travel without a car.

explanation.en: The whole passage explains induced demand: new capacity in busy cities fills up with new trips, so congestion returns. The other statements are either not claimed or too extreme (the author says new roads are sometimes justified).

Galileo and the Falling Stones

For nearly two thousand years, educated Europeans accepted the view, traced back to Aristotle, that heavy objects fall faster than light ones. The idea seemed to agree with everyday experience: a stone drops quickly, while a feather drifts slowly to the ground. Aristotle's physics was not based on careless observation, but it relied heavily on reasoning from general principles and on what could be seen without special equipment. Systematic experiment, in the modern sense, played little part in it.

The challenge to this view is usually associated with Galileo Galilei. According to a famous story, Galileo dropped two balls of different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa and showed that they reached the ground at the same moment. Historians, however, doubt that this event ever took place; the only account of it was written by one of Galileo's students many years later, and Galileo himself never mentioned it. Ironically, a similar experiment had already been performed in 1586 by the Flemish engineer Simon Stevin, who dropped two lead balls, one ten times heavier than the other, from a church tower in Delft and reported that they landed together.

What Galileo certainly did was two things that proved far more influential than any single dramatic demonstration. First, he constructed an elegant argument that exposed a contradiction in Aristotle's position. Imagine, he wrote, a heavy stone tied to a light one. If light objects fall more slowly, the light stone should hold back the heavy one, so that the pair falls more slowly than the heavy stone alone. But the two stones together are heavier than the heavy stone, so according to Aristotle they should fall faster. Since the combined object cannot fall both faster and slower, the original assumption must be wrong.

Second, Galileo studied motion by rolling balls down gently sloping ramps. Free fall was too rapid to measure accurately with the instruments of his time, but a ramp slowed the motion enough for him to time it, using a water clock. By measuring how far the balls travelled in successive intervals, he found that the distance covered increased with the square of the time, a mathematical relationship that held regardless of the ball's weight.

The significance of this work lies less in its conclusion than in its method. Galileo combined careful measurement, mathematical description and logical reasoning, and he treated experiments not as illustrations of ideas already believed but as tests capable of overturning them. The feather, of course, still falls slowly, because of air resistance, a factor Galileo himself recognised. The point was finally demonstrated in 1971, when an astronaut standing on the Moon, where there is no air, dropped a hammer and a feather and watched them land together.

to suggest that engineers were more skilled than philosophers
to show that Galileo copied his methods from another scientist
to point out that an experiment like the one in the famous story had in fact been carried out before

explanation.en: The author calls it ironic that "a similar experiment had already been performed" by Stevin. The point is that a drop test like the legendary one really happened earlier. Nothing says Galileo copied him, and historians doubt the tower story.
